Independent scored review of run r-20260915T050810199778-promotion-stops-authoring-the-record-the-worker-writes, plan reckon:crew-observability-truth §19. Reviewed commits 8bc1083 (fix(crew): skip the landing comment when the worker already wrote it) and 3049028 (docs: record the landing-comment dedup and its anchor). SCORE 89/100.

VERIFIED. (1) Gate claim reproduced independently: tests/test_crew_promotion.py at base be380283 = 40 passed, at the merged head = 42 passed, zero added failures, two tests added (37 to 39 functions). The reviewed run's own baseline/after logs carry the same 40 and 42. (2) Mechanism and intent match the plan's final record: promotion appends nothing when the run's committed plan already carries the run-derived comment id (git show <head_sha>:<plan> against the shared object store, computed before the idempotent already_recorded retry loop so post-merge re-promotion still resolves to already_recorded first). Only one c-run- id generation site exists in the source, and it is now guarded; no second append path bypasses it. (3) Evidence-doc counts verified: 20 anchor rows and 16 run-outcome rows match the amended 'twenty anchors / sixteen run-outcome comments' summary. (4) Self-hosting: this run's own worker-authored plan comment uses the very id the landing path now detects and skips, so the fix executed on its own landing; the manifest's commits list is in chronological order with the record-commit last, which the revisions[-1] read depends on.

FINDINGS. F1 (scope, minor): the commit introduces one new lint finding - F841 at tests/test_crew_promotion.py:1796, an assigned-but-unused 'path' local in the new _write_resource_html helper - a 'commit adds no findings' violation; all other ruff findings in the touched files are pre-existing backlog outside the changed lines. F2 (durability, minor): detection reads only the last declared commit, so a manifest listing commits out of order (or omitting the record commit) makes the guard miss and the duplicate-comment collision recurs silently; tests cover a single-commit worker only. Neither blocks the change. The merged-head suite attribution is intentionally out of this node's scope.

SCORES: goal_fidelity 19, evidence 18, scope_discipline 17, durability 16, fit 19; total 89/100.
